audit.whatIsWrong: The stun is discussed five times ('threatens the stun', 'eat the stun', 'if he lands the AoE stun', 'the stun chain starts here', 'chain stun + autos') and the page never says how it is produced. Mark of the Storm stuns after THREE applications - that is a counter you can watch, not a cooldown you guess at. Separately, 'his E slow' appears three times (early, whys[2], wants.foe[1]); Lightning Rush applies a mark and grants KENNEN Move Speed, it applies no slow. And the two layers disagree about the threat: the full layer calls Lightning Rush matchup-defining and says 'the stun chain starts here', while the content layer correctly points at Slicing Maelstrom.
audit.why: Counting to three is the entire matchup and it is completely absent. Every Thundering Shuriken, every Electrical Surge and every Lightning Rush pass adds one mark; at two marks on you, the next thing that touches you is a stun, and that is the moment to blink out rather than the moment to trade. Believing in a slow that does not exist makes you disengage in the wrong direction and mis-time the blink. And Lightning Rush is not where the chain starts - any of his three abilities starts it.
audit.corrected: The three-mark stun written into early, mid and the cooldown block as a count to watch; the fabricated E slow removed and replaced with what Lightning Rush actually does; the full layer re-pointed at the mark counter rather than at Lightning Rush alone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (P Mark of the Storm: 'Kennen stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities'; E Lightning Rush: 'pass through units and apply a Mark of the Storm. Kennen gains Move Speed')

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'track that cooldown and force the all-in when it's gone' about Slicing Maelstrom and never gives the number. Nothing else in his kit has one either.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom is a FLAT 120s at all three ranks - it does not shorten as he levels it, which is unusual and is precisely what makes 'force the all-in when it's gone' such strong advice: two full minutes with no answer, and the window does not shrink in the late game the way most ultimates do. Thundering Shuriken is 7/6.25/5.5/4.75/4s at 950 range against your 650. Electrical Surge is 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s. Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: The flat 120s written into late and the cooldown block with the point that it never shortens; the shuriken's 950-vs-650 range gap and the rest of his cooldowns added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Kennen six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while mid says 'Level 6 is where this lane flips', spikes[2] says 'you start blinking in to trade and threaten the kill', whys[5] says 'your blink-in trades start winning', late opens 'This is your game', and whys[3] says the 4-5 window is 'roughly even - neither side can commit a clean kill yet'.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 62.5% over 16 games and the prose describes exactly why: Kennen is a magic-damage poke champion into the one melee whose passive reduces magic and whose Q shields it, and he tapers off while Kassadin does not. Four separate strings say the lane has turned and the chart records none of it.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 set to Skill and Level 6, First item and 2+ items all flipped to Kassadin, in both layers. Levels 1-3 left with Kennen, which every source agrees on.
sources: content mid, spikes[2], whys[3], whys[5], late

audit.whatIsWrong: No itemization guidance against his damage profile anywhere.
audit.why: Electrical Surge applies on-hit magic damage and marks every few attacks, so his damage scales with attack speed and is magic rather than physical. Armour reads that trade completely wrong. Magic resist plus Void Stone is the answer, and it compounds with the Q shield in a way it does against almost no other top laner.
audit.corrected: Named in the interactions block: his damage is on-hit magic, so MR and Void Stone stack against it.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.tldr is the generic if-magic/if-physical boilerplate, and breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. The full layer also rates this HARD at 5.5/10 while the content layer calls it 'your game'.
audit.why: Kennen's whole kit is magic, so the conditional resolves to the favourable branch: Void Stone reduces it and the Q shield absorbs it, which is the structural reason a 62.5% win rate exists. Saying so plainly is worth more than hedging.
audit.corrected: tldr resolved to the actual case; silence removed. The HARD/5.5 label left alone - see notes.

edits.before: Kennen owns these levels outright — his Q bolt and Mark of the Storm autos out-range your Null Sphere, and he runs on energy while your Q drains a thin early mana pool, so he can poke effectively forever. Don't trade back into a full-energy Kennen; you'll just stack his marks, eat the stun, and walk into his E slow. Farm with the edge of Null Sphere, hug your side, and remember Void Stone already shaves 15% off everything he throws — you take this poke better than your health bar suggests.
edits.after: Kennen owns these levels outright - Thundering Shuriken reaches 950 against your 650, and he runs on energy while your Q drains a thin mana pool, so he pokes effectively forever. Count his marks: every ability he lands stacks one Mark of the Storm and the third stuns you, so at two marks the next thing that touches you is CC. Don't trade back into a full-energy Kennen. Farm at the edge of Null Sphere, hug your side, and remember Void Stone shaves 15% off everything he throws - his whole kit is magic.

edits.before: Level 6 is where this lane flips. Riftwalk finally gives you a way through his kite, and the instant you blink on top of him his entire AP kit hits your 15% reduction and your Null Sphere shield. Bait his Q bolt into that shield, R in, and Force Pulse him — he's squishy and his only outs are Flash or his ult. Respect Slicing Maelstrom: if he lands the AoE stun he chains marked autos on top of it, so commit your blink only when his R is down or you're healthy enough to survive it.
edits.after: Level 6 is where this lane flips. Riftwalk gives you a way through his kite, and the instant you land on him his entire AP kit meets your 15% reduction and your Null Sphere shield. Bait the shuriken into that shield, R in, and Force Pulse him - he's squishy and his only outs are Flash or his ult. Respect Slicing Maelstrom: it is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so commit your blink when it is down and simply do not commit when it is up. Keep counting marks the whole time - two is your cue to leave.

edits.before: This is your game. With Riftwalk maxed and Nashor's or Rabadon's online, you blink in repeatedly while his Q poke and empowered autos barely dent your Void Stone and shield, and an immobile Kennen has nothing to peel a stacked Riftwalk. He becomes a one-shot if you reach him before his R — the only thing that saves him is landing Slicing Maelstrom first, so track that cooldown and force the all-in when it's gone. Unlike a true scaling carry, Kennen tapers off; your 2+ item window only widens from here.

notes: THE COUNT WAS MISSING. Kennen's stun is discussed five times across the two layers and neither says how it happens: Mark of the Storm stuns after THREE applications, and every one of his abilities applies one. That is a counter on your health bar you can watch, not a cooldown you guess at - two marks means the next thing that touches you is CC, which is the real 'leave now' signal in this lane. FABRICATED EFFECT, three places: 'his E slow' (early, whys[2], wants.foe[1]). Lightning Rush applies a mark and grants KENNEN Move Speed; it has no slow. Believing in it makes you disengage in the wrong direction. LAYER DISAGREEMENT: the full layer names Lightning Rush the matchup-defining ability and says 'the stun chain starts here', while the content layer correctly points at Slicing Maelstrom. Any of his three abilities starts the chain, so I re-pointed the full layer at the mark counter. Added: Slicing Maelstrom is a FLAT 120 seconds at all three ranks - it never shortens, which is exactly why 'force the all-in when it's gone' is such strong advice and why the window does not close in the late game; the 950-vs-650 shuriken range gap; and the on-hit magic profile of Electrical Surge, which means magic resist rather than armour and compounds with Void Stone. Fixed: breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence; full.tldr was the generic if-magic/if-physical boilerplate when Kennen's kit resolves entirely to magic. LEVEL CHART: no stage read Kassadin on a 62.5% win rate while four separate strings said the lane had turned - Levels 4-5 set to Skill, Level 6, First item and 2+ items flipped to Kassadin. LEFT FOR YOU: the full layer labels this diff 'HARD' at 5.5/10 while the content layer calls it 'your game' and the data says 62.5%. I did not touch diff or the ratings because this champion's rating scale is internally inconsistent across the file, but HARD looks wrong here.
